title: Synaptic links had an uncertain relation to shared response changes in 193 Allen V1 cells
abstract: We tested whether detected synaptic links mark shared changes in movie responses between recording periods. We used matched anatomy and activity from 193 selected cells and 6,416 pairs in Allen V1 Deep Dive mouse 409828. A 1,203-second pause splits repeat 4. We excluded that repeat and compared three early repeats with four late repeats. The mean recording times differ by 29.06 minutes. We used distinct-repeat covariances and fixed cell scales. After cell and geometry controls, the event link coefficient was 0.000298 within periods and 0.007543 between periods. Their difference was -0.007245. Its central 95% movie-block range was -0.017789 to 0.002900. All single-cell and single-repeat deletions kept the event difference negative, but signs differed across sessions. The dF/F difference and the secondary input-cosine effect also had ranges across zero. Raw EM checks reproduced every direct count and input cosine. We supply code, compact inputs, all sensitivity scores, figures, source hashes and repeat instructions. One animal, selected cells, few repeats, data-derived scales and period-shared nuisance signals limit interpretation. The test does not establish a zero wiring effect or a causal mechanism.

display.caption: A pause splits movie repeat 4. Period-separated wiring coefficients remain uncertain in this selected one-mouse panel. Bars show conditional movie-block ranges. Reference assignments share the same observations.
The secondary shared-input model also gives uncertain change coefficients. Point checks show sensitivity to session, imaging planes, movie window and repeat grouping.
